passage.text: From a Gestalt perspective, symptoms are products of a creative self and reflect human uniqueness. Psychopathology therefore represents a unique creative adjustment to a difficult situation. When this adjustment becomes fixed, it stops serving the needs of the individual and their environment. It also narrows the individual's range of potentials. Symptoms are not viewed as separate, isolated items. Instead, they are seen as a narrowed spectrum of functions. They indicate that clients have limited flexibility in their reactions. As a result, these clients struggle to maintain fluid contact with their environment. They are unable to act according to their actual needs and potentials. Their behaviour and present experience are instead shaped by fixed patterns. They follow a habit rather than making a deliberate choice.

source.title: Article Aesthetic Diagnosis in Gestalt Therapy

taps.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
taps.correct: Symptoms become problematic when adaptive responses harden into rigid patterns limiting flexibility.
wrong: Gestalt therapy cures psychopathology by helping clients eliminate all symptoms.
Symptoms are isolated problems that require separate treatment interventions.
taps.explain: The text emphasizes rigidity and loss of adaptability, not elimination or isolation.

taps.context: As a result, these clients struggle to maintain fluid contact with their environment.
taps.explain: 'These' refers back to the subject—the clients with limited flexibility.

taps.context: When this adjustment becomes fixed, it stops serving the needs of the individual and their environment.
taps.correct: Fixed adjustments no longer meet the person's or environment's changing needs.
wrong: Adjustments that are fixed always harm both the individual and environment.
Individuals create fixed adjustments that intentionally ignore environmental needs.
taps.explain: The original emphasizes loss of function; wrong versions add judgment or intention.
